title: FraudLens
tagline: Finding the signal in rare financial fraud.
summary: A reproducible fraud-detection pipeline designed around class imbalance, temporal evaluation, and realistic review thresholds—not misleading accuracy alone.
challenge: With fewer than two frauds per thousand transactions, ordinary classification accuracy says almost nothing about whether a model is useful. The challenge was designing a meaningful evaluation that respected that imbalance.
approach: Validated the public benchmark data, removed exact duplicates, constructed a SQLite analysis layer, compared multiple classifiers, selected a threshold on validation data, and evaluated it once on a held-out chronological test split.
outcome: The selected Random Forest achieved 0.8179 PR-AUC and 81.75% F1 on its held-out evaluation. These results describe performance on a public benchmark, not production banking performance.

title: StudentPath
tagline: Predicting outcomes at the time decisions are made.
summary: A higher-education analytics system that distinguishes predictions at enrollment, after semester one, and with the full academic record.
challenge: Models claiming to predict student outcomes early can accidentally use academic information that did not exist when an intervention would have been possible.
approach: Created distinct feature sets for three decision stages, combined SQL exploration with reproducible sklearn pipelines, and documented class-sensitive evaluation and responsible-use limits.
outcome: Held-out accuracy increased from approximately 59.7% at enrollment to 71.9% after semester one and 75.8% with the full record. This is a demonstration using historical benchmark data, not an automated student decision system.

title: Mewar Market
tagline: A student marketplace with intelligence built in.
summary: A campus-oriented marketplace combining a full-stack commerce experience with explainable recommendations and fraud-risk screening.
challenge: Design a single student-facing product that supports useful discovery, listing management, and basic trust-and-safety flows.
approach: Built a React front end, Express backend and MySQL schema, with authenticated listings, search, saved items, recommendation rules and administrative review workflows.
outcome: A full-stack implementation with distinct user and administrative flows. No claim of production usage or a live deployment is made here.

title: Pediatric Malaria Screening
tagline: Exploring computer vision for health-related screening.
summary: An applied deep-learning exploration of early pediatric malaria screening using transfer learning and a Streamlit interface.
challenge: Explore how a computer-vision workflow might support preliminary image-based screening research while making its limitations explicit.
approach: Developed an experimental transfer-learning pipeline using MobileNetV2, TensorFlow and Keras, with an interactive application for demonstration.
outcome: A proof-of-concept machine-learning project, not a validated clinical diagnostic device.
